html:
The Cueva de las Manos, Cave of the Hands, is a rock shelter in Patagonia, southern Argentina, whose walls are covered with hundreds of stencilled hands, some made over 9,000 years ago.

Hunters of the guanaco, a wild relative of the llama, blew paint through bone tubes around their hands, leaving outlines in red, white, black and yellow. Most are left hands, many of them of young people. Other paintings show hunting scenes, with guanacos driven into traps, and patterns of circles and lines.

It is among the oldest art of South America, made by the ancestors of the peoples of Patagonia, long before the Inca roads and the gaucho frontier reached the north of what became Argentina. It became a World Heritage Site in 1999.
sum: The Cueva de las Manos, Cave of the Hands, is a rock shelter in Patagonia, southern Argentina, whose walls are covered with hundreds of stencilled hands, some made over 9,000 years ago.
